transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. Let's get started on the Tuesday webhook incident postmortem. As a reminder, we had duplicate webhook events delivered to some customers for 26 minutes, and the initial investigation points to a queue-worker deployment as the trigger. No permanent loss of payloads has been confirmed. Before I can sign off on the remediation register, I need final status from the backend, SRE, security, and support owners per our postmortem policy. Let's go through each area -- who wants to start?

transcript.text: I need to share something important I found just before this review. While tracing the worker deployment during a separate code review, I discovered an undocumented retry shortcut that bypasses the webhook idempotency key on the second attempt. I confirmed this behavior only shortly before this meeting, which is why I haven't filed the remediation ticket yet. This is very likely the root cause behind the duplicate events we saw on Tuesday.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share something relevant for the SRE status. While checking an unrelated alert migration, I discovered that the duplicate-delivery alert has been disabled for ten days. I also confirmed that the correct alert threshold for this service should be 15 minutes, not whatever it was effectively running at -- which likely explains why the incident ran for 26 minutes before being caught. I haven't updated the monitoring ticket yet, but this needs to be addressed as part of the remediation.
